one_month_reasoning: The window ends at the Oct 30 close (Nov 1 is a Sunday). I now think the Q3 2026 print most likely falls just after it: Booking announces its webcast date about four weeks ahead (Sep 30, 2025 for the Oct 28, 2025 print; Jul 7, 2026 for the Aug 4, 2026 print), and as of Oct 2 neither EDGAR (last 8-K Aug 4) nor the company press-release feed (latest item Sep 29, a Lola product release) shows a Q3 notice. Aggregators estimate ~Nov 3. I put P(print in window) at ~15%. Events inside the window are the Oct 27-28 FOMC (after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%), oil and Middle East headlines, and more AI-agent news (Meta Muse partnerships), plus Expedia/Airbnb prints that are also likely early November. With no scheduled company event, I dropped the expected-beat tilt and the earnings widening. The distribution is a near-lognormal with median ~$159.6 and sigma ~10.8% (38-39% realized vol / ~3.5, which already includes the September Muse headline days). It is mixed 85/15 with a wider 14% component for the chance that the print lands inside the window, which slightly fattens the tails. The ~22% drop since Aug 31 ($199.09) could revert, but momentum is negative, so I take no directional view.

bull.story: Travel normalizes as ME impacts fade, transformation savings ($650M by end-2027) land, and AI partnerships prove additive; the multiple re-rates to ~18-19x NTM $13.5.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$118 the stock would be ~9.5x FY27 consensus EPS ($12.37), ~10x my FY27 $11.85 and an ~11-12% FCF yield, and ~21% below the $150.14 52-week low (intraday May 20, 2026). Trading there would most likely mean estimates are falling (room nights turning negative, the marketing ratio jumping as AI agents disintermediate, a large parity-damages award, or a travel recession from the oil shock), not just multiple noise.
